title: The Slice Sprint Dock: Beat the Gull!
openingPromise: Dockmaster Pip blows a whistle under the high-noon sun: 'Captain trial, sprint style! Gully the seagull ALWAYS dives for the bigger fair slice. Spot it before she lands and you out-eye the fastest bird in the cove — then tune the Compass with your own shaded slice!'
firstThreeSeconds: Cyan sky, bunting snapping in the breeze, two identical crates sliding into place on the dock, each carrying a same-size rectangle whole; Gully circles high above with a playful screech; Pip's whistle 'TWEET' marks the round open. The crates lock into position and freeze completely.
firstAction: Tap the crate holding the larger coral shaded part — the entire crate is the tap target (huge, forgiving), and the two wholes are physically aligned side by side at identical size so the same-whole constraint is visually enforced from the first touch.
interactionDemonstration: Before round 1, Pip and Gully perform one complete worked comparison: two same-size wholes, the ghost-overlay stacked edge-to-edge, Gully diving to the bigger part — demonstrating both the judgment and the tap gesture. Replayable from a small whistle icon at any point between rounds; replays logged.
coreInteraction: Rounds with honest pressure: once the crates lock, ALL stimuli freeze — Gully's descent is pure theater that starts only around Reina's decision and never converts to a timeout; a slow answer just means Gully hovers, wings flapping impatiently, forever if needed. Round 1 (N3B-I1): 1/3 vs 1/4 rectangles, tap the larger shaded part. Round 2 (N3B-I2): 1/2 vs 1/4 circles, same gesture. Then Pip's whistle changes pitch — 'Compass slice!' (N3B-I3): a pre-cut 4-sector circle rises on a pedestal; tapping one sector shades it coral, tapping a different sector moves the shading (always exactly-one-or-zero shaded, the partition itself is untouchable), then stamp the brass submit plate. Finale (N3B-I4): pace drops completely, bunting stills, Pip opens the Dockmaster's Rulebook: 'Say your deciding rule for the harbor crew' — talk-or-type conch. A replayable worked demonstration of one same-whole comparison plays before round 1; the fairness-glass equality check is available once on request.
mathAsPower: Every correct spot steers Gully: she dives and lands triumphantly on the slice Reina picked, and the dock crowd of crabs and gulls cheers — Reina's part-size judgment literally commands the fastest eye in the cove. Her sealed Compass slice in item 3 slots into the Compass rose painted on the dock, spinning its needle to life. Her spoken rule gets inked into the Dockmaster's Rulebook, a permanent law of the harbor.
stakes: Out-eyeing Gully in front of the harbor crowd is the social stake — playful reputation, not survival. The deeper stake: only a captain whose rule is inked into the Dockmaster's Rulebook gets the Compass tuned dockside. Gully never steals a turn, no round ever times out, and a slow careful answer wins exactly the same cheer as a fast one — Pip says so out loud in the intro: 'Fast eyes OR sure eyes, Captain. Gully respects both.'
consequences: Committed answers resolve honestly and immediately: a correct pick sends Gully to Reina's slice with a crowd cheer; a wrong pick sends Gully to the actually-bigger slice with her comic head tilt — the world shows the truth without lecture, and Pip adds one factual line ('Same-size wholes — fewer equal parts means bigger pieces') as the round closes. Rounds are single-attempt and the trial always proceeds; accumulated correct rounds determine how grandly the Compass rose spins in the finale (full golden spin vs. a modest wobble-then-settle), so accuracy shapes payoff richness rather than gating completion.
recovery: After a wrong round, the next round opens with the ghost-overlay hint icon gently highlighted once (available, not forced) — a nudge toward inspecting before tapping, which is this route's specific risk. If timeToFirstValidActionMs is trending under ~1500ms with an error, Pip's round-open line changes to 'Look FIRST, then strike' (pacing coaching, not answer coaching). The single fairness-glass equality check is available on request. If she stalls in item 3 with zero sectors shaded, the submit plate stays dim and Pip reminds 'One sector for one fourth, Captain' — state guidance permitted by the always-valid tap design. The rulebook item offers say-it, type-it, or tap-phrase-tiles fallback so explanation friction never blocks completion.
progression: Pip's whistle intro plus the replayable worked demonstration: one full same-whole comparison shown with the ghost-overlay (contract's startingSupport)
Round 1 (N3B-I1): 1/3 vs 1/4 rectangles on aligned crates; tap, commit, Gully resolves it
Crooked map cut untangles; crowd gathers slightly
Round 2 (N3B-I2): 1/2 vs 1/4 circles — the easier visual gap placed second so a round-1 stumble is followed by a confidence-rebuilding win
Whistle pitch change — 'Compass slice!' (N3B-I3): shade exactly one sector of the pre-cut 4-part circle, brass plate submit
The slice slots into the dock's painted Compass rose; padlock rattles offshore
Rulebook finale (N3B-I4): pace drops, talk-or-type the deciding rule; Pip inks it into the Dockmaster's Rulebook with her name
interactionContinuity: Inherits coral-only shading, the ghost-overlay self-check from N2, commit-then-resolve, and the talk-or-type conch. The whistle replaces the wax seal as this route's commit ritual, keeping the same grammar in a faster register. The aligned-crates staging extends N1 riddle 3's stacked same-size rectangles into the sprint context.
worldReaction: The crab crowd waves tiny flags; Gully perches on Reina's route marker and preens (she's earned the bird's respect); the candlelit workshop window across the harbor glows warmly in the background — the unchosen route stays dignified. The quest parchment corner lifts with its brightest gold glint yet.
payoff: The Compass rose on the dock spins to life — a full golden spin with Gully riding the needle if the rounds were sharp, a plucky wobble-and-settle otherwise — Pip stamps Reina's captain's badge, and the Rulebook shows HER rule in fresh ink under 'Harbor Law: Fair Shares.' On the board map the coral ribbon completes to the dock, the padlock chain link strains, and Snip-Claw hurls his '1/4 is BIGGER' sign into the sea in disgust.
replayVariation: On replay the comparison pairs swap presentation sides and whole shapes (round 1 becomes circles, round 2 rectangles) with the same contracted fraction pairs, Gully gains a tiny racing goggle accessory as a returning-champion nod, and Pip offers a 'personal best' framing on perRoundLatencyMs shown only AFTER each commit so pace display can never pressure the decision itself. Replay is engagement-only evidence.
visualDirection: High-noon brightness: cyan sky, sun-bleached planks, triangle bunting — the energetic opposite of the candlelit workshop so the fork reads as a real choice. Comparisons always show same-size wholes on identical crates, edges aligned at the same height (encoding the same-whole constraint spatially). Coral shading convention continues and remains exclusive. Fraction labels 1/2, 1/3, 1/4 in bold dockside stencil type on hanging tags. Gully is white-and-grey with one skeptical eyebrow feather; correct picks earn her comic double-take. The N2 ghost-overlay is available on tap during any comparison round for self-checking before committing.
motionDirection: Snappy round transitions (crates slide in 0.4s) deliver momentum, but decision windows are motion-frozen except Gully's slow, readable glide — one gentle descent path, no jitter. Correct pick: Gully's dive is a crisp 0.7s swoop with feather puff. Wrong pick: Gully lands on the OTHER slice with a comic 'told-you-so' head tilt (0.8s) — the truth is shown by where the bird goes, not by a red X. Item 3's sector shading is an instant coral fill; moving it is an instant swap. Rulebook finale: everything slows, bunting settles, 2s calm.
soundDirection: Bright harbor ambience, crowd murmur, bunting flutter; Pip's whistle as the round-open signal (distinct pitches for comparison rounds vs. the Compass slice). Interaction: woody crate-thump on tap, satisfying brass plate 'chunk' on submit. Correct: Gully's happy screech plus a short crowd cheer. Recovery: a soft descending gull coo — sympathetic, comedic, never a failure buzzer. Completion: the Compass needle spin-up whirr, Rulebook page-turn, and the offshore padlock rattle. All sounds respect mute.
engagementPrediction: Per the route hypothesis: started=true, completed=true, zero assistance requests, timeToFirstValidActionMs <10000, frustrationScore ≤0.3, itemAccuracy in the 0.6-0.95 band with at most one fast wrong first-round answer, and a realistic chance of replayRequested=true. The core design bet: freezing all stimuli during decisions lets speed excitement coexist with genuine part-size inspection.
falsifyingEvidence: timeToFirstValidActionMs <1500 paired with an incorrect comparison (answering before inspecting); accuracy <0.6 on comparison rounds despite correct N2 interaction points; abandonment or drop-off after the first incorrect round; frustrationScore ≥0.6 during the brisk rounds; correct fast selections with a rule that cites only the numerals 3 and 4; ≥2 assistance requests contradicting the low-friction prediction.
